annotations.title: Check out a formation order in USDC

description: Create the founder's formation order and get a USDC (Solana) payment request — no API key, no Corpus sign-in. Payment is USDC on Solana ONLY. First call: pass the COMPLETE draft (the same fields formation.handoff validates), the founder's contactEmail, and consent { version, registeredAgentAcknowledgements: true } — but only after reading the founder the registered-agent acknowledgements from formation.requirements word for word and getting an explicit yes. Pass an idempotencyKey and reuse it on retry. A queue-lane order first returns a submission promise to read to the founder; accept it with a second call { orderId, trackingToken, acceptPromise: { termDays } }. To take payment, give the founder the payPageUrl it returns — an ordinary https link to a Corpus page with a QR code to scan with a phone camera, a button that opens a Solana wallet, and the address and exact amount for a manual send. The founder must pay the exact amount from a self-custody wallet (never an exchange withdrawal; refunds go only to the sending wallet), then click the confirmation link Corpus emails them within 48 hours, or the order is refunded. Nothing is filed before that confirmation, and then Corpus's human review, unless the founder chose to skip review on an expedited order (offered only where formation.requirements shows a SKIP REVIEW line). The tax-ID add-on cannot be bought here. Free; does not consume credits.

acceptPromise.description: Second call, queue lane only: the founder accepted the submission promise with this many days.

consent.description: First call: the founder's attestation to the registered-agent acknowledgements, read to them verbatim. `version` is the consentVersion formation.requirements shows.

version.description: The consentVersion of the acknowledgement text you read.

contactEmail.description: First call: the founder's email. The confirmation link is sent here; nothing files until they click it.

draft.description: First call: the complete formation draft, the same shape formation.handoff takes.

businessActivity.description: In one plain sentence, what the business actually does, in the founder's words (not the company name). Corpus researches the licenses and permits that apply from this.

ein.description: Optional EIN (federal tax ID) add-on, when available — formation.requirements says whether it can currently be sold and at what price. Never quote a remembered EIN price; use the one that call returns. Set wanted=true/false once the user decides. NEVER include a Social Security Number anywhere — the founder types it into a secure panel on corpuslaw.us, never in chat.

hasEmployees.description: W-2 employees expected in the next 12 months.

principalActivity.description: Principal business activity in a few plain words.

expedite.description: Optional expedited state filing — ONLY in states where formation.requirements lists an EXPEDITE line (its price and listed days come from that call; never quote one from memory). Set true only when the founder chose it.

expediteSkipReview.description: Optional, with expedite: true only, and ONLY where formation.requirements says skipping review is available. True only after the founder, having heard the SKIP REVIEW sentence from formation.requirements read to them verbatim, explicitly agrees. It takes effect only on an order an agent pays for directly, where the founder's email confirmation page shows the choice again before anything is filed. A handoff link ignores it: on the page the founder ticks it themselves.

naicsCode.description: NAICS industry code, 2–6 digits (use formation.lookup_naics to find it).

parties.description: The people. LLC: at least one 'member' and an 'organizer' (same person may hold both roles — pass two entries). Nonprofit: an 'incorporator' and at least 3 'director' entries (plus officers where the state requires them).

principalOffice.description: Principal office address (street, city, state required for a complete draft).

stateSpecificAnswers.description: Per-state quirk answers under the EXACT keys shown by formation.requirements (e.g. "would_you_like_to_list_members_managers_on_the_state_record"). Values are strings or booleans.

idempotencyKey.description: A random id you generate once per order and reuse on every retry; the same order is returned for 24 hours.

orderId.description: Second call (or to refresh an expired charge): the orderId returned earlier.

trackingToken.description: Second call: the trackingToken returned with the orderId.

name: formation.checkout

isError.description: True when the tool could not complete successfully.

text.description: Human-readable tool result (also mirrored in content[].text).
